In summary, our research is concerned with

a) the synthesis of (3R)-1 from (3R)-2-hydroxy-1-phenylpropane, (3S)-1 from (2S)-2-phenyl-1,3-propanediol and (3R)-4 from (R)-1,2-propanediol; b) the separation of the enantiomers of 1,4 and their conversion into (2S)-4 and (2R)-4, respectively, and

the development of efficient synthetic routes to enantiomerically and diastereomerically pure target compounds, which are used as reference compounds for the determination of enantiomeric and diastereomeric ratios of the naturally occurring substances by chiral gas and/or liquid chromatography.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enantiomeric composition of (3R)-1 in the pheromone of H. bajulus is 98:2 (S:R) and that of (2S, 3R)-4 and (2R. 3R)- 4 in the pherome of P. sanguineum is 95:5 (S:R).
we were able to identify the sex pheromone of the longhorn beetle Pyrrhidium (Pyrrhiza) sanguineum as (3R)-hydroxy-2-henxanone and the sex pheromo of Hylotrus bajulus as 2,3-henxanediol.
(3R)-1, (2S, 3R)-4 and (2R3R)-4 are the major pheromone compounds of H. bajulus and P. sanguineum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the male pheromones of these beetles are enantiomeric mixtures of 2,3-hydroxyhexanes.
the enantiomers of 2,3-hexamol and 2,3 hexanediol are readily separated on a commercially available chiral stationary phase (Chirasil-Dex).
it is possible to synthesize enantiopure compounds from readily available starting materials and that the enantiomers can be separated by GC on a chiral column.
